(1) a multi-scale contractiveness can be used to improve facial expression recognition accuracy by reducing the effects of the pose of the image; and (2) a contractive discriminative analysis can be used to learn a representation of the image that separates out the emotion-related features from those related to the identity and pose of the subject, improving facial expression recognition accuracy further.

we have developed a semi-supervised learning approach that combines a convolutional neural network with a contractive auto-encoder to learn a feature representation that is invariant to pose and identity, while being discriminative of emotion, achieving the best reported accuracy on facial expression recognition in images.

we propose a semi-supervised approach to solve the problem of facial expression recognition using recent ideas from deep learning to deal with factors of variation in data.
the CCNET is able to capture the pose variations, the CDA is able to capture subject variations, and the combination of both is able to capture emotion variations.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the factors of variation can be disentangled in a semi-supervised way, and that this is a promising approach for emotion recognition in images.

a combination of unsupervised and supervised learning can lead to better results in emotion recognition, and that a contractive feature learning approach can help to disentangle the factors of variation in the data.
